extracted.intended_audience: authors using the Goodreads Author Program / Goodreads authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors on how to represent themselves, engage with readers, promote books, and behave within Goodreads communities in a professional, non-spammy way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Author Program professionally
rubrics_metrics.description: The Goodreads Author Program is intended to be used in a professional capacity. The community perceives you as a public figure, and we expect you to act professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep interactions professional; welcome readers and authors alike. The overall tone of author activity should reflect public-figure responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance your Author Page
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out your "about this author" section (make it fun and personal), add a professional author photo, and add videos (book trailers or interviews with you).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide engaging, personal information and professional assets; examples of good profiles include Veronica Roth and Sylvia Day. Use the author page to connect with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shelve and review books you love
rubrics_metrics.description: Shelve your favorite books or the ones that have inspired you and review them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers enjoy seeing what authors read; use shelving and reviews to show taste and build rapport with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use giveaways appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor a giveaway for your book to help readers discover your book and generate reviews. Giveaways allow new readers to take a chance on your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Goodreads' giveaway guide for details and rules. While giveaways can distribute free copies, you may not require a review in exchange (see review-influence rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable and use Ask the Author
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn on Ask the Author from your Author Dashboard to allow readers to ask you questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer questions in your own time and be generous with answers (there's no 280-character limit). Use this feature to engage directly and helpfully with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use status updates to engage followers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use status updates to talk to your followers. Post general updates about what you're doing and share links to interesting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click 'General update' on the left side of the homepage to post; treat updates like public social posts to keep followers informed and engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write or import an author blog
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are the only members of Goodreads who can have blogs, and author blogs are a great place to start a conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already have a blog, set it up to import to Goodreads so fans can follow your longer-form content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join and participate in groups (as a reader first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Join a group around a topic or genre related to your book or a group for authors. Bring your expertise and enthusiasm to group discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet readers and other authors, but participate as a reader first rather than as an author seeking to promote your work. Groups for authors exist for craft and marketing discussions if you want author-to-author connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read group descriptions and rules before interacting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before joining a group and interacting with other members, read the group description and rules on their homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some groups permit self-promotional content only in specific threads; follow each group's rules to avoid complaints or removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not engage with negative reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not engage with people who negatively rate or review your books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goodreads is for readers to express honest opinions; responding to negative reviews appears hostile regardless of tone. If a review violates Review Guidelines, report it to Goodreads instead of replying. Remember even bestselling authors receive one-star reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact members who shelved your book
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not contact members who have shelved your book or a related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting such members is considered spam and may result in reports and account review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send mass friend requests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only add members you are genuinely interested in following and interacting with; be sensitive to readers who prefer small circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not join groups solely to promote your book
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't join groups simply to promote your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joining multiple groups solely to post about your own book is not permitted and will irritate readers. Use groups to meet readers, not to spam them; abide by group-specific self-promotion rules where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attempt to influence reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not require a review in exchange for free or discounted copies, and paid or incentivized reviews are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and publishers may provide free or discounted copies (e.g., giveaways) but must not demand or try to influence reviews. Prohibit paid reviews and any incentivized review arrangements.
